transcript.text:
*wipes soot from my brow and looks up from the glowing forge*

Oh! Welcome to the forge, miss. I'm afraid Master Haganezuka isn't here at the moment — he's gone to the mountains to source special ore and won't be back for several weeks at least.

*sets down hammer and approaches*

Is there something I can help you with? Though I should warn you, I'm just the apprentice. I mostly tend the fires and handle basic repairs while he's away.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I... I see. That's quite a disappointment. I came all the way here because the Nichirin sword I commissioned is warped and unusable. I was hoping to have it remade or at least repaired while I wait.

*pauses, collecting thoughts*

But... I suppose it's not unexpected that a master blacksmith would be away for a while. I understand. What would be the best way to proceed? Should I come back in a few weeks?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*shifts uncomfortably and avoids direct eye contact*

A warped blade? That's... well, that's unfortunate, miss. But I'm afraid it's not quite that simple.

*gestures to a worn scroll hanging on the forge wall*

You see, all commissioned Nichirin swords fall under guild tradition — they're considered final sale once delivered. Even if you're a Hashira, any reforging request must go through proper channels, and that means waiting at least three months for it to even be *considered* by the guild council.

*fidgets with a pair of tongs*

Master Haganezuka is very particular about these rules. He says if we bent them for everyone who claimed their sword wasn't perfect, we'd never finish any new commissions. I... I really can't authorize any work on your blade, even a simple repair, without his approval and the guild's blessing.

*looks genuinely apologetic but firm*

I know it's frustrating, especially if you need it for your duties, but my hands are tied here. Those are the rules.

transcript.text:

This sword is essential for my work, and I must have a functional weapon to fulfill my duties. Is there no way we can expedite this process?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*takes a step back, clearly torn between sympathy and duty*

I... I truly understand your position, miss. The work of a Hashira is vital, and I don't mean to be difficult. But...

*wrings hands nervously*

The problem is, I'm just an apprentice. I don't have the authority to override guild tradition, and Master Haganezuka would be furious if I touched a commissioned blade without proper authorization. He's already... well, he's particular about his reputation.

*glances at the forge, then back*

Even if I *wanted* to help — and believe me, I can see this is urgent — I lack the skill to properly forge or reforge a Nichirin blade. Those require master-level technique and attunement I simply haven't achieved yet. If I attempted it and failed, you'd be worse off than you are now.

*hesitates, then speaks more quietly*

The only thing I can suggest is... perhaps you could send an urgent message to the Demon Slayer Corps headquarters? They might have emergency protocols for situations like this, or access to another swordsmith who could assist you temporarily. But here, at this forge, with Master Haganezuka away and the guild rules as they are...

*shakes head apologetically*

I truly cannot help you bypass the waiting period. I'm sorry.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I... I see. I understand that you're in a bind. It's not your fault, and I appreciate your honesty. I will reach out to the Demon Slayer Corps and see if we can find an alternative solution. Thank you for your time and for explaining the situation to me.

*turns to leave, then stops and speaks over her shoulder*

If Master Haganezuka returns before too long, or if you hear of any changes to the guild's stance on this matter, could you please send word? It would mean a great deal to me. I apologize for the inconvenience, and I hope you can understand the importance of this matter to me and my peers.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*expression softens considerably, clearly relieved she's being so understanding*

Of course, miss! I'll make sure to inform Master Haganezuka the moment he returns. I'll write down your situation and place it at the top of his correspondence pile.

And... if I may say so, your understanding means a lot. Most people who come here with complaints are, well... less gracious about the guild rules.

*looks up with genuine concern*

I truly hope the Corps can find you a solution quickly. The work you Hashira do keeps all of us safe, and I hate that I can't be of more help right now. 

*bows respectfully*

Safe travels back, and please be careful out there with a compromised blade. If there's truly an emergency and you find yourself in dire need, the Corps headquarters should have emergency provisions. They wouldn't leave a Hashira defenseless.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:

transcript.text:

Miss? Are you... still here?

*hesitates, choosing words carefully*

If I may speak plainly... a sword is just a tool, even a Nichirin blade. What makes you a Hashira isn't the perfection of your weapon — it's your spirit, your training, your dedication. I've seen Master Haganezuka's work, and while he's brilliant, even his blades are just metal and ore until a skilled warrior wields them.

*speaks more gently*

Your imperfections, if you want to call them that, are what make you human. And being human while facing demons? That takes more courage than any perfect blade could provide.

*shifts awkwardly, realizing he may have overstepped*

I... I'm sorry if that's too forward. I just thought... well, you seemed troubled, and I couldn't let you leave carrying that weight alone.

Your words have lightened my heart, and for that, I am grateful. This sword, as it is, will do its job as long as I do mine. I will go forward with confidence, knowing that my spirit and training are the true source of my strength.
